Unit 1 - Shell, Bash and the Automation Mindset
Why This Matters
Before writing scripts, you must understand what the shell is, why Bash exists, and how commands become
repeatable automation. This prevents the common beginner mistake of memorising syntax without
understanding execution. Core Concepts
Concept
Explanation
Shell
A command interpreter that accepts input, expands it,
invokes programs, and returns status information. Bash
The Bourne Again Shell. It is widely available on Linux
servers and is commonly used for operational
automation. Script
A text file containing commands and shell language
constructs that are executed in sequence. Interpreter
The program that reads and executes a script. The
shebang selects it. Exit status
Every command returns an integer status. Zero usually
means success; non-zero indicates a failure or special
condition. Idempotence
Running an automation repeatedly should produce the
intended state without causing duplicate or destructive
side effects. Worked Examples
Your first script
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "Hello from Bash"
Run it safely
chmod +x hello.sh
./hello.sh
echo "$?"
Inspect Bash
echo "$BASH_VERSION"
command -v bash
getent passwd "$USER"
How Companies Use It
Companies use Bash for bootstrap scripts, deployment helpers, health checks, backup jobs, CI/CD glue code,
operational runbooks, and emergency remediation. Bash is excellent for orchestrating command-line tools. Large application logic is normally better implemented in Python, Go, Java, or another general-purpose
language.

Explanation

Most shell bugs come from incorrect quoting, word splitting or accidental glob expansion. Mastering variables

Concept
Explanation

Allow parameter and command expansion while
preventing most word splitting. Command substitution

Unit 4 - User Input, Arguments and Options
Why This Matters
Scripts become reusable when they accept validated inputs rather than depending on hard-coded values. Core Concepts
Concept
Explanation
read

$1, $2 and so on contain arguments. Special parameters

shift

getopts
Parse short command-line options reliably. Usage function

Arguments

All arguments

Input prompt

e) environment="$OPTARG" ;;
v) verbose=true ;;

Concept
Explanation

Why This Matters
Conditions allow scripts to make safe decisions based on files, strings, numbers and command outcomes. Core Concepts
Concept
Explanation

fi

branch="feature/login"

fi

Unit 8 - Loops and Repetition
Why This Matters
Loops automate repeated work across files, hosts, services and API results. Safe loops must handle spaces,
failures and empty inputs. Core Concepts
Concept
Explanation
for loop
Iterate over a known list or generated sequence.
while loop
Repeat while a condition or command succeeds.
until loop
Repeat until a condition becomes true.
break and continue
Control loop flow. C-style loop
Useful for counters: for ((i=0; i<3; i++)). Read loop
while IFS= read -r line; do ...; done is the safe text-
reading pattern. Worked Examples
Arguments loop
for host in "$@"; do
printf 'Checking %s\n' "$host"
done
Read file safely
while IFS= read -r host || [[ -n "$host" ]]; do
[[ -z "$host" || "$host" == \#* ]] && continue
printf 'Host: %s\n' "$host"
done < hosts.txt
Retry loop
attempt=1
max=5
until curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/health >/dev/null; do
(( attempt >= max )) && exit 1
sleep "$attempt"
((++attempt))
done
